paragraphs.text: Malvos , called the Sifter , was a Sangrazul brought to the plane Cridhe by the planeswalker Tempé .

When he arrived on Cridhe , Malvos was a big, muscular man tattooed with Tempé 's marks. He had bushy red eyebrows and green eyes. A Finder, he was adept at locating leylines . He earned his nickname, "the Sifter", due to his ability to tell the truthfulness of others' speech. At the time of the Parting, he disguised himself as a metal trader and wore gaudy silk from the plane's Southern Isle. He later served as the apothecary of the Felonarch, the leader of the Nohrish. After 520 years stranded on the plane, he grew obese, gorging on cream and honey pies instead of feasting on mana. By the time of his death, he weighed 300 pounds.

The Planeswalker Tempé found Malvos as a child, employing him as a Finder and promising to teach him to become a Planeswalker himself. He traveled to Ilcae and Parnash , meeting Planeswalker enemies of Tempé along the way.

Malvos stole Tempé's mana as payment for his services. He was punished with exile to Cridhe , a plane known to be almost devoid of mana, and marked with snake tattoos on his arms which would come alive and kill him if he thought about touching mana.

He traveled across Cridhe to finally appear on its mainland, where he found an enormous source of mana hidden even from Planeswalkers' eyes: the Clan Tree of Cridhe . Malvos planned to find a suitable person, teach them magic, and then give them all mana from the Clan Tree of Cridhe so that they would become a planeswalker and both could escape the plane. Malvos wanted to travel to Ilcae , where he could find other planeswalkers like Platon or Krim . In exchange for information on Tempé's mana lines, they would set him free from the snakes-tattoo curse.

His plan was simple but needed time. Eventually, he found a suitable person - Nohr , who was able to do magic which caused a stir between him and other people of his clan. Malvos made Nohr drunk and gave instructions on how to use the magical sword Soulslayer, which he had stolen from Tempé, to become a planeswalker and leave the hated place. Unfortunately for Malvos, something went wrong. Magical rays from the sword missed the mana line, and the Clan Tree was destroyed, causing the Parting , with the land splitting in twain and the island's people being separated by the new fissure. In this way, Malvos brought an age of darkness upon the plane which would last for 520 years.

In 4064 AR , when the Nohrish raiding party returned from Inys Haen without the Keeper and with the young Aylith instead, Malvos assisted Nazir in investigating the failure. He played a key role in the deception that allowed Nazir to pose as a servant and interrogate Aylith under that guise. Throughout the growing unrest in Inys Nohr, Malvos remained a steady force, ensuring Nazir’s physical and mental stability, even as rebellion simmered around them.
paragraphs.section: The Mending of the Clan Tree

paragraphs.text: As the uprising reached its peak, Malvos accompanied Nazir to Inys Haen, hoping to force the Awakening Ritual before their enemies could mount a counterattack. However, the plan unraveled when Aylith’s allies arrived, turning the battle against them. When Nazir attempted to flee, Malvos remained behind to control the situation, refusing to believe his master had abandoned him. His arrogance proved to be his downfall.
paragraphs.section: The Mending of the Clan Tree

paragraphs.text: In the chaos, Feryar the Fool confronted Malvos. Startled at the elf's sudden change of personality, Malvos instinctively reached for his sword, only to realize too late that it was Soulslayer — the cursed blade that the Planeswalker Tempé had long ago decreed would be his doom. As he grasped the hilt, the silver serpents embedded in it came to life, sinking their fangs into his flesh, sealing his fate. Gravely wounded, he was found by the Nohrish and taken prisoner, where he was forced to instruct Jedhian in the ways of magic to save his own life. Jedhian’s intervention spared Malvos, but at the cost of the artifact blade itself, which crumbled to ash in the process.
paragraphs.section: The Mending of the Clan Tree

paragraphs.text: Though he survived, Malvos was left crippled and abandoned following the Mending of the Clan Tree . He wandered the wastelands of Cridhe, forsaken by his former allies. In his final moments, his old mistress, Tempé, reappeared, demanding to know the location of the plane’s mana. Malvos, weary and broken, gave what little he knew before dismissing her. Smirking, she left him to his fate. Unbeknownst to him, his tent was, in truth, a hungry shroud , a magical entity that lured him to sleep before collapsing around him, devouring him whole.
paragraphs.section: The Mending of the Clan Tree

paragraphs.text: Tempé won the magical firesword Soulslayer from the Thorn in a duel. Malvos stole the sword from Tempé, taking care not to touch it with his bare hands as the planeswalker had marked the artifact. The iron blade was patterned with intertwined snakes in flowing mixed metals, and the pommel was made of silver snakes that twined together, a silver cord holding a gem on each side that contained their own magic. One of the stones, a saphirron crystal, was a cure for the blade’s wound, to be used one time only, rendering the sword inert afterward. The other stone held a crystal that, when added to water and poured over the blade, would restore the sword's powers. Though the blade appeared dull and rounded, it could cleave rocks and shoot frozen bolts of blue fire. Malvos gave the sword to Nohr to instigate the Parting , but it was lost soon after. The tip of the sword broke off in the struggle, ricocheting and lodging above Nohr's heart. Soulslayer was rediscovered over 500 years later by Jedhian , lost again, and found again by Lorris , who gave it to Arn , who gave it back to Lorris, who threw it to Jedhian, accidentally giving it to Nazir instead. Nazir ran Aylith through with the blade but failed to kill her before he was attacked by a mob, slaying over 30 before he fled. After Malvos touched the blade, invoking his curse from Tempé, he used the second gem to heal himself, destroying the sword in the process.

Malvos states that "Finders can be Walkers", and Tempé promised to teach the young Sangrazul to planeswalk. It is unclear if this means Malvos was an ember , if there was only a chance that he could become a Planeswalker, or if Tempé simply lied about his potential.
